note: Twenty-one Arena gave Scilla as their last residence at Ellis Island. Among them an ORAZIO Arena (20 April 1904, aged 26) and four men named Rocco.

Fifteen Donato gave Scilla as their last residence -- which settles one thing outright: the Donato were unquestionably a Scilla family by the 1890s, whatever the birth registers of the 1850s do not say.
Six Polistena, including a married couple and two teenagers.
Four Costa. No Generosa among them.
Fourteen Melluso gave Briatico as their last residence, including two different Filippo.
Thirteen Anile, five of them on one ship on one day.

SOUGHT, NOT FOUND. The 1900 census puts a LORENZO COSTA, 24, in Rocco Arena's household -- a Costa, in the household of a man who married a Costa. Six hundred and seventy-four Lorenzo Costa are indexed across all American ports and NOT ONE gives Scilla as a last residence. Either he came under another spelling, or he arrived before the Ellis Island index begins in 1892, or he came through a port whose lists are thinner.

SOUGHT, NOT FOUND FROM SCILLA. Seven hundred and twenty-seven Antonino Arena are indexed and the Scilla ones are not among them; the name belongs overwhelmingly to Messina and Palermo. Antonino Arena born in New York in 1902 would only appear here if he travelled to Italy and came back, which no record yet says he did.
